messages:
maria: Quick update — completed AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 sweep on opti-13b for chat+completion workloads. Posting high-level numbers and proposed canary/fallback policy.

sam: Nice. TL;DR?

maria: p95 latency (hosted, 2k tokens): AWQ-int8 188ms, GPTQ-int8 215ms, FP8 175ms. Token cost reduction: AWQ ~42%, GPTQ ~36%, FP8 ~48%.

kevin: Quality deltas? Which eval sets?

maria: Eval harness: assist (conversational), code-gen, and long-context wiki. AWQ mean EM drop ~0.9%, GPTQ ~1.3%, FP8 ~1.7% on code tests. On long-context QA, AWQ shows slightly better coherence in some seeds.

sam: Can you paste the eval command you used?

maria: ```python
# eval snippet
run_eval(model='opti-13b-awq-int8', dataset='redwood-assist', seeds=3, n_ctx=2048)
```

maria: Notes: AWQ has higher variance across seeds (one seed +0.2% EM), and we caught a tokenizer padding mismatch when switching to private infra — fixed in awq-patch-3.

deploy-bot: Canary started: hosted/opti-13b-awq-int8 -> 5% traffic (us-west). Triggered by CI:quant-sweep-2026-03.

kevin: Suggested automatic rollback triggers: EM_delta > 1.0% (absolute vs baseline) OR error_rate +0.5% absolute OR p95 latency > baseline * 1.3. Agree?

sam: Add an additional check: false_positive_rate (hallucination flagged by eval annotator) +0.7% should also trigger fallback.

maria: Agreed. For hosted/dedicated/private we propose these profiles:
- hosted: {quant: "awq-int8", fallback_to: "gptq-int8", fallback_threshold_em: "1.0", max_p95_pct: "130", canary_steps: "5,25,50,100"}
- dedicated: same but with canary windows longer (45m) and allow manual approval to promote beyond 50%
- private: mirror config but auto-promote disabled by default; require customer opt-in.

kevin: Prefer the keys be explicit in config: `quant_profile`, `fallback_policy.fallback_to`, `fallback_policy.em_threshold`, `slo.max_p95_pct`, `canary.schedule` — we should validate these on deployment.

maria: Canary plan: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%, with 30m evaluation windows and automated checks against the eval-set + sampled user logs. If any check fails, auto-fallback to gptq-int8 and open #incidents with a summary. Manual override allowed by infra-admins.

sam: For dedicated infra, also add region-aware fallback: if us-west overloads, route to eu-central gptq variant before global rollback.

ops: small ask — add metric: delta_in_conversational_turns (measure drop in follow-up correctness). We've seen quantization break multi-turn more than single-turn metrics capture.

maria: Good call. We'll add `multi_turn_em_delta` to the regression checks.

maria: I'll push the canary policy YAML to infra-config PR after I tidy up the thresholds and include the runbook steps.

sam: Can you link the runbook when you push?

maria: Gist/runbook: https://go/redwood/gists/quant-canary-runbook — TL;DR: manual rollback, automated fallback, metrics: EM_delta, false_positive_rate, multi_turn_em_delta, p95_latency, error_rate, and visual sampling of 50 user sessions per window.

deploy-bot: Canary promoted -> 25% (no regressions detected in 30m window).

kevin: For private customers, do NOT auto-promote beyond 25% without explicit customer consent. Record consent in CMDB.

maria: Noted. I'll add consent gating and notify solutions-eng on promotion. Planning to kick off dedicated canary tomorrow US morning. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

sam: Nice work — keep notes and we'll do a 24h watch after full rollout.
